full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to making of the reference, in brief, were that one Abu Baker Siddique alias Siddique Ali Pramanik instituted Criminal Case No. 990C of 1977 against one Zillur Rahman Sarker in the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Bogra who transferred the same to Atmuli Union Council for adjudication as it was found that the case was triable by the village Court under the Village Courts Ordinance, 1976. Zillur Rahman Sarker filed a petition before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate under section 15(1) of the Village Courts Ordinance for transfer of the said case and the Sub-Divisional Magistrate on the basis of that petition called for the records from the Village Court and stayed further proceeding of the case. But before the stay order was communicated to the Village Court the Village Court had passed a unanimous judgment decreeing the case in favour of Abu baker Siddique. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate set-aside the judgment, withdrew the case and transferred the same to the Court of Mr Manzur Ali, Magistrate, 2nd Class for trial on the basis of his order dater 31-1-78. Hence Abu Baker Siddique filed a Motion in the Court of the sessions Judge. Who made this reference. 

 3. The point of law involved in this reference is whether the decree passed by the Village Court before it got intimation of the stay order passed by the learned Sub-Divisional Magistrate is nullity or it is required to be set by a competent Court. Mr Gaziul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Abu Baker Siddique has referred before me the case of Rani Elarshamukhi Sinha vs Maharaja Dasi Kanta Acharjee Chowdhury and others reported in 7 DLR 473. A Division Bench constituted with Ahmed, J and Guha, J delivered the judgment. Ahmed, J took the view that all orders and judgments of a Court of law either of the Court of first instance or of the Appellate Court or of the Court of revision are good and valid orders from the time of their pronouncements. If any step is taken by any Subordinate Court having ordinary normal jurisdiction in ignorance of any order of a superior Court, the subsequent orders passed by the Subordinate Court are not ipso facto null and void. These orders may be irregular or even illegal but they will stand unless they are either recalled or at the instance of the party concerned, are set-aside. Guha, J also took the same view. It is observed by him that it cannot be said that the moment an order for stay of proceedings is pronounced by the superior Court that operates as. Staying the hands of the trial Court and makes all sections and proceedings taken by the trial court as nullities and without jurisdiction, no matter whether the trial court had ant notice and any knowledge of the action taken by the appellate court. The effect of the order for stay passed by the superior Court is an order of trial court in contravention of the order for stay is irregular or at the most illegal but not 'ultra vires' and a nullity. In the case of Md Majibur Rahman Mia vs Jamini Mosahar and others reported in 7 DLR page 82, referred to by Mr Gaziul Haque similar view has also been taken. In that case it is observed "the order giving delivery of possession by the executing Court after the order issued by the High Court staying delivery but before it was communicated to the executing Court followed by actual delivery of possession may be invalid and irregular but it cannot be said to be void ab initio and ultra vires, and until and unless that illegal and invalid order is set-aside in that proceeding it cannot be challenged in a separate suit or in a separate proceeding. Mr Mashiul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing to oppose the reference has cited before me the case of Mohamed Sher Khan and others vs Charninkan Khan and another reported in AIR 1926 Allahabad page 456 wherein it has been held that a sale held in ignorance of the order for stay passed by an appellate Court is without jurisdiction and must be set-aside. He has also referred before me the case of Raj Bahadur Singh vs Pirthipal Singh and others reported in AIR 1942 Oudh page 24 wherein the view has been taken that the stay order passed by a High Court takes effect from the date in which it is pronounced and not on the date on which it is communicated. A sale held despite the passing of such a stay order even though the same is not communicated is ultra vires. In the present case the Village Court had initially jurisdiction to make adjudication in the case and it seems to me that as it passed the decree before intimation about the stay order passed by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate the decree passed by it will not be nullity and the decree may be an irregular and an illegal decree but it will have to be set-aside by a competent Court. This view taken by me is supported by the two decisions of the 7 DLR referred to by me above. As the decree passed by the Village Court is a unanimous decree, there being no provision for appeal against the decree, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate had no jurisdiction to hear appeal against the decree and, as such, he was incompetent to set-aside the same. Moreover, as the case had already been disposed of he had no jurisdiction to withdraw the same from the Village Court and transfer it to another Criminal Court for trial, under the provision of section 15(1) Village Courts Ordinance.
